source_row.society: Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh
source_row.extraction_instructions: Drupal listing at /events paginated ?page=0..2 (~12/page, 33 events total across exactly 3 pages, no further pages seen). Each card and each detail page carries repeated 'icon-detail-item' chips (calendar/clock/monitor=online/map-pin=venue/CPD lozenge image) giving date, time, format and CPD deterministically; hybrid events fold 'Hybrid: Online and <venue>' or '<venue> & Online' into the map-pin text alone with no separate monitor icon, so venue text must also be scanned for the word 'online'. Detail pages are tabbed (#overview/#programme/#fees/#further-information, sometimes #live-links); fees are plain label|£X tables inside #fees with no preceding <h2-4> heading (the 'Fees' label is a tab link), so the shared pricing_tables.py heading-detector misses them entirely — this extractor parses the #fees tab's own tables directly. Sold-out events show 'Fully Booked' text in place of the Book-now button (event-notification-text class).

registry_comment: RCPE — Drupal /events listing, page_query pagination, deterministic icon-chip dates/venue/CPD + #fees tab pricing (bypasses pricing_tables.py's heading requirement)

concerns: Listing includes 'College Meetings & Ceremonies' category events (MRCP(UK) Diploma Ceremonies) — real dated/venued/bookable events but not CPD content. Kept them (not clearly junk per the brief's skip criteria) but the team may want a category-level filter if these don't belong in a CPD directory.

'External Events' category (e.g. Scottish Cardiac Society AGM, Scottish Thoracic Society Symposium) are third-party society events booked via Eventbrite widgets on an RCPE-branded page, not RCPE's own events — included as-is since they appear in RCPE's own /events listing.

Recon's expected_found list included 'RCPE Online Education', 'MRCP PACES Preparation' and 'Acute Medicine Updates' — none appeared across all 3 listing pages (33 events, confirmed no page 3 exists). They may simply have no scheduled upcoming instance right now; nothing to fix in the extractor.

venue coverage in the 12-event detail sample is low (4/12) because most of RCPE's near-term events are the online Evening Medical Updates series — expected given the site's current programme mix, not an extraction gap (verified by hand against several online-only detail pages).

pricing_tiers missing on only 1/12 sampled events ('Modern Medicine: Parasites') — verified by hand: no #fees div and no £ anywhere on the page, so [] is correct (genuinely free/no fee info published), not a miss. Diploma Ceremony's fee is plain prose ('free of charge' + 'a charge of £35 per guest') rather than a table — a small regex fallback handles that pattern specifically; it won't generalise to other prose phrasings if RCPE varies the wording later.

Minor cosmetic artefact: a few fee labels on the site wrap a single trailing letter in its own inline tag (e.g. 'low or lower-middle income country'); the shared regex-based tag-stripper (same approach as rcsed.py/rcpsych.py) turns that into 'countr y' with a stray space. Price and the rest of the label are correct — cosmetic only, not worth a source-specific patch.

Audit-gate fix (2026-09-23), 2 defects: (1) individual Evening Medical Update pages (frailty, confusion, weight-loss, etc.) open their Overview with a verbatim block-booking promo for the whole EMU series and close with an equally generic 'programme' paragraph — neither is event-specific. Added `_strip_emu_boilerplate()`, applied before both the LLM prompt and the deterministic fallback, so descriptions now come from the per-event 'Learning outcomes for this Evening Medical Update include: ...' text only. (2) medical-trainees-conference-2027 has a genuine, currently-open abstract call (Clinical Lesson + QI/Audit case-report submissions, deadline 9am 11 Nov 2026) that the shared abstract_classifier's deadline-capture regex missed because RCPE phrases it as 'deadline for ALL submissions is' (classifier only recognises 'deadline for submissions is'), so it fell through to the classifier's conservative no-parseable-deadline default of False. Added an RCPE-local text normalisation (before calling the shared classifier, which was left untouched per the no-shared-file rule) plus <script>/<style> stripping before the abstract-gating text is built. Net effect: abstract_open is now True with the real deadline 2026-11-11 for this event, which I believe is factually correct (a live, dated call for submissions) rather than a false positive — worth a product-level check-in if the intent was to exclude student/trainee-only case-report competitions from `abstract_open` on purpose, since that would need a different, narrower rule than the one requested.
